correctness.rationale: For the labeled sunlet S_n=C_n circ K_1 with n>=3, proper strong odd coloring has a degree-three neighbor multiset either monochromatic or rainbow. A proper rim coloring therefore admits exactly one pendant extension at a two-step backtrack and q-3 extensions otherwise. The q(q-1)-state transfer on ordered unequal rim colors has eigenvalue a=1+(q-3)(q-2); two centered color-space eigenvalues whose power sum U_n satisfies U_0=2,U_1=3-q,U_{j+2}=-(q-3)U_{j+1}+(4-q)a U_j; and symmetric/antisymmetric zero-row/column eigenvalues +/- (4-q) with multiplicities q(q-3)/2 and (q-1)(q-2)/2. The trace yields F_n(q)=a^n+(q-1)U_n+q(q-3)(4-q)^n/2+(q-1)(q-2)(q-4)^n/2. Equality for q>=3 and polynomial interpolation handles nonnegative q<3. This gives χ_so(S_n)=2 even n,4 odd n; optimal named-colorings 2 even and 3^n-3 odd. Independently enumerated 20 (n,q) cases, n=3..6 and q=3..7, against formula; inspected independent source transfer and original-definition verifiers. Finite enumeration does not replace spectral proof.

evidence: Strong odd means every color in each open neighborhood has odd multiplicity; for a degree-three rim vertex, this gives the all-equal/all-distinct dichotomy.
For named colors, the cycle-corona enumerator differs from standard proper chromatic polynomial by weighted backtracks.

originality.rationale: Known strong odd coloring upper bounds for unicyclic graphs include χ_so<=4 outside C5. This chromatic upper bound covers one consequence but not the complete all-palette named-assignment polynomial, spectral recurrence, or exact optimal-coloring multiplicity. The weighted sunlet rim transfer is not an ordinary chromatic polynomial evaluation because q>=5 choices depend on two-step backtracking. Inspected Caro et al. Proposition 2.2 and related Kwon/Park source identification; no exact sunlet polynomial found.

value.rationale: The sunlet is a canonical unicyclic corona with a local parity-coloring rule, and the full strong odd coloring polynomial is a natural exact enumerator. The closed transfer decomposition determines every palette count, parity-dependent chromatic threshold, and exponential growth without a case-by-case census.
